extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and newspaper industry professionals (wartime public)
extracted.subtask_description: A front-page newspaper collection of wartime news: government economic regulations affecting industry pay, industry conservation measures, criminal/trial reporting, and military communiqués intended to inform the public and industry stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary limitation to $25,000
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall receive a salary of more than $25,000 a year after deductions for Federal income taxes on the 'whole salary' and certain other allowable deductions; sweeping regulations limit salaries to $25,000 a year after certain deductions beginning January 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations issued by James F. Byrnes applied to both private and public salaries except those fixed by statute. The President asked that his own $75,000 salary be so trimmed despite statutory exception. The freeze of all salaries and wages up to $25,000 and disallowance of increases applies except where increases are approved by the War Labor Board or Treasury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deductions allowed in computing $25,000 limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed deductions in computing the $25,000 salary limitation include Federal income taxes on the whole salary, 'customary' charitable contributions, and certain payments on life insurance policies and other fixed obligations (including past income taxes due).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Byrnes said 'customary' charitable contributions meant those the recipient had been making (text notes prior-year contributions). Allowances for life insurance payments and other fixed obligations were permitted only where the recipient has no other source of income which can be utilized for these purposes and only where the recipient can show that payments cannot be met without disposing of assets at a substantial loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted salary increases without prior War Labor Board/Treasury approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain increases do not require prior approval of the War Labor Board or Commissioner of Internal Revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types permitted: individual promotions or reclassifications; individual merit increases within established salary rate ranges; operation of an established plan of salary increases based on length of service; increased productivity under incentive plans; operation of a trainee system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified ban on increases for salaries $5,000 or less (effective Oct. 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified ban on increases in salaries of $5,000 or less was made effective as of Oct. 3; the $25,000 limitation takes effect Jan. 1, 1943.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the $25,000 limitation is effective Jan. 1, 1943, increases in salaries at this level without Treasury approval are forbidden before that date. The qualified ban on increases at the $5,000 level was effective immediately on Oct. 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: War Labor Board and Treasury jurisdiction over salary increases
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Labor Board was given control over increases in salaries (notably those in excess of $5,000), and the Treasury was given jurisdiction to pass on other salaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations disallowed salary increases except those approved by the War Labor Board or Treasury. The Treasury interpreted its role to mean it would pass on salaries under $5,000 being paid to employees in executive, administrative, or professional capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper industry conservation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for newspapers to conserve scarce materials and labor included decreasing the number of editions published and eliminating sample copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The industry committee discussed conserving newsprint, transportation and labor through decreasing the number of editions, eliminating sample copies and other measures; the committee expected to organize formally and included widely known publishers, business managers and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: News disclosure / censorship principle (Senator Byrd)
rubrics_metrics.description: In wartime the public 'should be told the whole truth about the war, the good and the bad, except when the truth would aid the enemy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senator Harry Byrd criticized some wartime censorship as 'very foolish and unwise' and argued the government owes the people truthful reporting except where disclosure would aid the enemy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice/limit on publication of casualty lists
rubrics_metrics.description: At present, publication of Navy and Marine casualties by any one newspaper is limited to those men within the base circulation area of that newspaper; Senator Byrd advocated that all casualty lists should be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contrasts an expressed policy/practice limiting casualty publication to local-area servicemen with a normative call to publish all casualty lists unless security concerns intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for conviction of concealing a saboteur (treason-related concealment)
rubrics_metrics.description: For defendants charged with concealing the Nazi saboteur and handling money knowing of sabotage schemes, if convicted the penalty will be fixed by the court; minimum five years, maximum death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes that for those charged with concealing the saboteur the court will fix the penalty within statutory bounds; in the reported case the minimum is five years in prison and the maximum is death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for misprision of treason (Hedwig Engmann indictment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conviction under the misprision of treason indictment carries a maximum penalty of seven years imprisonment and a fine of $1,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grand jury returned an indictment charging 'having the knowledge of the commission of treason without reporting it to the authorities' (misprision of treason); the specified maximum penalty is noted in the reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal-trial procedural notes (jury selection and custody)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jury selection may include a panel mix (example: nine women and three men in one treason trial); defense may request jurors be kept in custody until verdict; court may extend session times and hold Saturday hearings to speed trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are procedural actions described in the reporting of a treason trial: selection of a jury, defense requests regarding juror custody, and the judge's measures to accelerate proceedings (longer sessions, Saturday hearings).
